claims.text: For CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Si, Mn, or Al, formation and persistence of a protective oxide above 900 °C is governed by selective oxidation of X.
Al has a high oxidation affinity in the stated alloy systems.
Selective oxidation of Al promotes a continuous and coherent surface oxide.
The Al-promoted oxide is mechanically compatible with and adherent to the alloy substrate.
The protective Al-containing scale may consist of Al2O3 or a related spinel- or corundum-type phase.
An adherent Al-containing oxide layer prevents further high-temperature degradation.
Mn has a lower oxidation affinity than Al or forms oxides that are less mechanically compatible with the substrate.
Mn-containing surface oxides are unstable and prone to cracking.
Mn-containing surface oxides are prone to spallation.
Oxide-layer continuity and coherence depend on formation of a structurally compatible spinel- or corundum-type surface phase.
CrFeCoNiAl-type alloys will retain an intact protective oxide during long-term high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn-type alloys will develop less stable oxide layers that crack or spall under the same exposure.
An alloy lacking Al or containing substantially less Al will form a less protective and less stable oxide than an Al-rich comparison alloy under identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies to oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at lower temperatures or in inert atmospheres.
Multiphase microstructures and competing oxidation reactions may alter the proposed protective behavior.
